texts.preamble: Jai Mata Di Swasahayata Samuh Through ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 February, 2026 Author: Hirdesh Bench: Anand Pathak, Hirdesh Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Gwl:5875 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Anand Pathak & Hon'Ble Shri Justice Hirdesh On The 13th Of February, 2026 Writ Appeal No. 430 of 2026 Jai Mata Di Swasahayata Samuh Through President Rajkumari Bai Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others Appearance:
texts.arguments: 2. It is contended on behalf of appellant that the learned writ Court has failed to conduct a proper judicial review under Article 226 of the Constitution of India to assess whether the administrative decision was illegal, irrational, or procedurally improper. The writ petition was dismissed based on generalized observations rather than addressing the substantive issues, such as the lack of evidence proving that the food served was unhygienic or caused harm to any child. The reliance on W.A. No. 1477/2019 (Abhishek Swa Sahayata Samooh) was misplaced due to a lack of factual parity with the present case. The use of disposable plates (Dona/Pattal) was necessitated by water scarcity, not poor food quality. The learned writ Court ignored NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:5875 2 Jai Mata Di Swasahayata Samuh Through ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 13 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101553746/ 1 WA-430-2026 significant discrepancies in the records between the Government Primary School and the Government Middle School. These inconsistencies affect the validity of the action taken. This omission violates principles of fairness and reasonableness. 3. On the other hand, learned Counsel for the State submits that the order of learned writ Court is well-founded, legally sound, and requires no interference by this Court.
